items.title: Toshiko Akiyoshi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: because of Lew’s job with the Tonight Show, he went to Los Angeles and out from boredom he remembered that I had four charts, so he suggested he would get the musicians together and we rehearsed every Wednesday morning... So that’s how it started.

ctx.x: Pianist and composer. And I’ll make a quote from the All Music Guide to Jazz that called you “one of the top arrangers of the last 25 years.” And I suspect that you might have preferred that they call you a composer?

I think probably because in my case both is the same. I don’t really — as a rule — I don’t arrange somebody else’s music. I have done a few numbers of Lew’s. I’ve done two to the exception, one Dizzy Gillespie one, and another one, Frank Wess was with the band for ten years. It was my gift to him along with his tune. Other than that I don’t do that stuff.
That’s an interesting scenario to write an arrangement for someone who’s a great arranger themselves.

items.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: that was Lew, and that‟s the first time I met him, and then I said, “I want to cop him for my concert.” ... So that was the first time, actually this was the first time we played together, quartet.

ctx.x: How was the feeling with the other musicians, how…?

Oh, they were very supportive. Of course, they knew how nervous I was, you know. So … they were very, very, very supportive. I‟m grateful for that. And it‟s just uh … I don‟t really remember anything, because I really nervous, and I was like that. But, I was playing a lot before that, you know, before this happened, so I had no problem playing, and once you‟re playing it‟s fine, but before you‟re playing, you get really nervous. But it was, you know … so, it went like that and…. Lew, sometime, a long time ago,…
